1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and appear as short separate lines rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column with large controls and good spacing that remain readable at mobile width.

4.why: Copy such as 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.' and 'Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready' is short and plain.

5.why: The verification-code field explicitly shows the placeholder example 'Example: 123456'.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long paragraph; all instructional text is brief.

7.why: No long authenticator secret or backup codes are shown, so no copy-to-clipboard control for such secrets appears.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any screen.

9.why: Standard email and password fields are present and should work with browser autofill and password managers.

10.why: Step indicator, clear headings and prominent blue primary buttons make the current step and main action obvious.

11.why: After a code is sent the screen presents both 'Check code' and 'Send a new code' together, so more than one action is available.

12.why: Green banners plainly state outcomes such as 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: Users can resend a code, retry entry and continue without penalty, as shown by the persistent 'Send a new code' option and error recovery.

14.why: The error 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' states the problem and the fix without blame.

15.why: Messages say 'Enter it when you are ready' and no countdown or expiry timer is visible on any screen.
